Toyota Brings Fresh Adventure-Ready Concepts at the 2026 SEMA Show Under the Woodland Banner
7 photos
Photo: Toyota Motor Corporation
At the 2026 SEMA Show , the Japanese automaker's Toyota Motor North American division is bringing all sorts of things, including of the Woodland variety, as it turns out.
The TMNA division has been pretty busy as of late, showcasing the latest 2027 model year changes for a raft of popular models like the Camry, Corolla Cross, or the Grand Highlander, which just received its own Woodland Edition. But they’re also keeping an eye on everything else, revealing their Toyota Battery Center of North America in Saline, Michigan, claiming the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series Manufacturer’s Championship for the fourth time in its history, or Mazda Toyota Manufacturing achieving the one-million vehicle milestone.
Well, since it’s early November, they’re also ready to come to Las Vegas, Nevada, for the 2026 SEMA Show and, so far, have revealed ahead of the event’s official dates of November 3-6 a little something for everyone. Although it’s not the skiing season just yet, Toyota has already prepared for it with the Snowhunter family of concepts, imagining a complete track-equipped range consisting of five models: Tundra, Tacoma, 4Runner, Land Cruiser, and Sequoia.
Aside from the body-on-frame trucks and SUVs reimagined for deep-snow travel, there was also the GT-S Performance Concept, a reimagining of the Toyota Crown Signia crossover SUV as a “sleek grand touring machine that blends everyday space and comfort with the attitude and road feel of a true sports car.” But that’s not all, of course.
As such, meet the ‘Woodland Vision,’ a family of Woodland concepts that “reimagine how a variety of electrified and family-focused vehicles can be equipped for life beyond the pavement.” There are new versions of the RAV4, Grand Highlander, Sienna, bZ, and Crown Signia ready for prime time, all ready to abandon the city streets at a moment’s notice for “trailheads and campsites.”
CALTY Design Research was in charge of establishing “a cohesive visual and functional identity for the Woodland concepts,” with common elements like “lift kits, large over-fenders, rugged satin-black wheels, All-Terrain tires, two-tone paint on the roofs and hoods, roof racks, and cross bars.” All of them are also dressed in the same Horizon Blue paint, which is inspired by Toyota’s hues from the 1960s used on the Stout, Crown, and Corona.
Set apart, the RAV4 Woodland Plug-in Hybrid Concept and Sienna Woodland Concept reveal Toyota’s electrified and family-focused vehicles taking on a more “adventurous role” within the household; the Woodland bZ Concept brings the Woodland theme into Toyota’s battery-electric lifestyle, and the Grand Highlander Woodland Concept plus the Crown Signia Woodland Concept aim for both “refinement and versatility.”
“United by a shared design language and a common spirit of exploration, the Woodland concepts imagine a future where more vehicles are ready to leave the pavement behind and make the journey itself part of the story,” explains the company, the motivation behind the new concept series.
